words.gloss: one whose army is superior to his

hindi: बलवान् द्वारा आक्रमण किया गया दुर्बल राजा उससे श्रेष्ठ सेना वाले का आश्रय ले, जिसे दूसरा मन्त्रशक्ति से न छल ले।
english: A weak king, attacked by a strong [one], should resort to [one] whose army is superior to his, whom the other would not outwit by power of counsel.
notes: Subject of the first clause is the weak king; tad in tad-viśiṣṭa-balam = the strong attacker (his army is the one exceeded). atisandadhyāt = outwit (glossary); the optative with na is rendered 'would not'; a sense 'could not' is possible. mantra-śakti = power of counsel (6.2).

words.gloss: of [those] of equal powers of counsel
of [one whose] excellence is under control

hindi: समान मन्त्रशक्ति वालों में विशेषता अधीन सम्पत् वाले से अथवा वृद्धों के सम्पर्क से है।
english: Among [those] of equal powers of counsel, the distinction [is] from [one whose] excellence is under control, or from connection with elders.
notes: No verb in the Sanskrit; bare copula supplied. āyatta-sampadaḥ is ambiguous (ablative 'from one whose excellence is dependent/under control' or genitive); āyatta = dependent on, under control; the exact sense (excellence in one's own hand, or dependent on another) is not certain. vṛddha = elder (alternative: the aged/grown). samyoga = connection (glossary 4.7 'saṃyoga = connection'); the e-text writes samyoga with m before y, as it writes sambhūya, sandhi (e-text habit, not flagged).

words.gloss: in the absence of a superior army
by the powers of counsel and of might

hindi: श्रेष्ठ सेना के अभाव में समान सेना वालों से अथवा समान सेना वाले संघों से मिलकर बलवान् के विरुद्ध खड़ा रहे, जिन्हें मन्त्र और प्रभाव की शक्तियों से न छल ले।
english: In the absence of a superior army, [he] should stand united against the strong [one] with [those] of equal army, or with saṅghas of equal army, whom [the strong one] would not outwit by the powers of counsel and of might.
notes: balavataḥ is read as ablative/genitive singular, 'against the strong [one]' (alternative: accusative plural 'the strong ones'). yān (plural) is taken to refer back to the allies of equal army (sama-balaiḥ, saṅghaiḥ), the unstated subject of atisandadhyāt being the strong king; this reference is not certain. saṅgha is kept as saṅgha (glossary 11.1), here a group; the political sense is not implied. prabhāva = might (9.1), kept apart from śakti = power; the dual instrumental is the dvandva 'powers of counsel and of might'.

words.gloss: of [those] of equal powers of counsel and of might

hindi: समान मन्त्र और प्रभाव की शक्ति वालों में विशाल आरम्भ से विशेषता है।
english: Among [those] of equal powers of counsel and of might, the distinction [is] from vast undertaking.
notes: Bare copula supplied. ārambha = undertaking, enterprise.

words.gloss: in the absence of an equal army
by the powers of counsel, might and energy

hindi: समान सेना के अभाव में हीन सेना वाले, पवित्र, उत्साही, विरोधी बने हुओं से मिलकर बलवान् के विरुद्ध खड़ा रहे, जिन्हें मन्त्र, प्रभाव, उत्साह की शक्तियों से न छल ले।
english: In the absence of an equal army, [he] should stand united against the strong [one] with [those] of inferior army—pure, energetic, [who have] become adversaries—whom [the strong one] would not outwit by the powers of counsel, might and energy.
notes: As in unit 3. śuci = pure (alternatives: honest, loyal). pratyanīka-bhūta = who have become adversaries (of the strong one, understood; not stated).

words.gloss: of [those] of equal power of energy
from acquisition of one's own battle-ground

hindi: समान उत्साह-शक्ति वालों में अपनी युद्ध-भूमि के लाभ से विशेषता है।
english: Among [those] of equal power of energy, the distinction [is] from acquisition of one's own battle-ground.
notes: Bare copula supplied. lābha = acquisition (13.5).

words.gloss: from acquisition of one's own time of battle

hindi: समान भूमि वालों में अपने युद्ध-काल के लाभ से विशेषता है।
english: Among [those] of equal ground, the distinction [is] from acquisition of one's own time of battle.
notes: Bare copula supplied.

words.gloss: of [those] of equal region and time
from draught animals, weapons and armour

hindi: समान प्रदेश और काल वालों में युग्य, शस्त्र, आवरण से विशेषता है।
english: Among [those] of equal region and time, the distinction [is] from draught animals, weapons and armour.
notes: yugya = yoked animal or conveyance (draught animals/vehicles); the exact sense is not certain, Hindi keeps युग्य. āvaraṇa = covering, rendered 'armour' (alternative: protective coverings in general). deśa = region (glossary 4.3). Bare copula supplied.

words.gloss: in the absence of a helper
obstruction of ration, fodder, fuel and water

hindi: सहायक के अभाव में दुर्ग का आश्रय ले, जहाँ शत्रु, प्रचुर सेना वाला भी, भोजन, चारा, ईंधन, जल की रुकावट न करे और स्वयं क्षय और व्यय से युक्त हो।
english: In the absence of a helper, [he] should resort to a fort where the enemy, even with an abundant army, would not make obstruction of ration, fodder, fuel and water, and himself would be joined with loss and expenditure.
notes: The subject of kuryāt and yujyeta is the enemy (amitraḥ). yujyeta (passive optative of √yuj) = 'would be joined with'; the sense 'would meet with loss and expenditure' is natural. bhakta = ration (9.2); yavasa = fodder; uparodha = obstruction.

words.gloss: from accumulation and the place of retreat

hindi: समान दुर्गों में संचय और अपसार से विशेषता है।
english: Among equal forts, the distinction [is] from accumulation and the place of retreat.
notes: Bare copula supplied. nicaya = accumulation (stores); apasāra = the place of retreat (10.2). tulya-durgāṇām could also be a bahuvrīhi 'of [those] with equal forts'; the plain reading 'among equal forts' is taken.

words.gloss: endowed with accumulation and the place of retreat

hindi: “क्योंकि संचय और अपसार से सम्पन्न मनुष्य-दुर्ग की इच्छा करे,” ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: “For [one] should desire a human fort endowed with accumulation and the place of retreat,” says Kautilya.
notes: manuṣya-durga rendered literally 'human fort' (alternatives: fort of men, i.e. a fort constituted by men, as against a natural fort; man-made fort); the sense is not settled here. Formula 'iti X' = '..., says X' (glossary 12.1). Subject of icchet unstated, '[one]'.

words.gloss: of the neighbouring chief, forest chief, member of his family and prince in disfavour
by supporting the party of the seducible
by applications of weapon, fire and poison
afflicted by loss, expenditure and absence from home
by destruction of the supply line, reinforcements and foraging force
by allies, forest tribes and armies
skilled in battle on low ground, in pits and at night
free from hindrance of the road
to be approached by great loss and expenditure
from abundance of forts, forests and places of retreat
of the exertions of the army

hindi: उसका आश्रय ले इन कारणों से — “पार्ष्णिग्राह, आसार, मध्यम अथवा उदासीन को प्रस्तुत करूँगा; सामन्त, आटविक, उसके कुल का सदस्य और निकाले गए राजकुमार — इनमें से किसी एक के द्वारा उसका राज्य हरवाऊँगा अथवा मरवाऊँगा; अथवा कृत्य-पक्ष को सहारा देने से उसके दुर्ग, राष्ट्र या स्कन्धावार में कोप उत्पन्न करूँगा; अथवा शस्त्र, अग्नि, विष के औपनिषदिक प्रणिधानों से इच्छा के अनुसार पास वाले को मारूँगा; अथवा स्वयं अधिष्ठित योग-प्रणिधान से इसे क्षय और व्यय तक पहुँचाऊँगा; अथवा क्षय, व्यय, प्रवास से सन्तप्त उसके मित्र-वर्ग या सेना में क्रम से उपजाप प्राप्त करूँगा; अथवा रसद, सहायक सेना, प्रसार के वध से उसके स्कन्धावार की रोक करूँगा; अथवा सेना को पास लाने से उसके रन्ध्र को उठाकर पूरे समूह से प्रहार करूँगा; अथवा प्रतिहत उत्साह से इच्छा के अनुसार सन्धि प्राप्त करूँगा; अथवा मुझ में बँधे हुए के सब ओर से कोप उठ खड़े होंगे; अथवा आसार-रहित उसके मूल को मित्र, आटवी, सेना से नष्ट कराऊँगा; अथवा बड़े प्रदेश के योग और क्षेम की यहाँ रहते हुए रक्षा करूँगा; स्वयं बिखेरी हुई अथवा मित्र द्वारा बिखेरी हुई मेरी सेना यहाँ रहने वाले की एक स्थान पर खड़ी असह्य होगी; अथवा निम्न, खात और रात्रि के युद्ध में निपुण मेरी सेना मार्ग की बाधा से मुक्त पास वाले में कर्म करेगी; अथवा प्रतिकूल प्रदेश और काल में यहाँ आया हुआ स्वयं ही क्षय और व्यय से नहीं रहेगा; बड़े क्षय और व्यय से पहुँचने योग्य यह प्रदेश है, दुर्ग, वन और अपसार की बहुलता से; दूसरों के लिए रोग-प्राय, और सेना के व्यायामों के लिए जिसकी भूमि प्राप्त नहीं है; आपत्ति में पड़ा हुआ उसमें प्रवेश करेगा, अथवा प्रवेश कर चुका बाहर नहीं निकलेगा।”
english: That he should resort to for these reasons: “I shall produce the heel-seizer, the reinforcer, the middle king or the neutral king; by any one of the neighbouring chief, forest chief, member of his family and prince in disfavour, I shall have his kingdom taken away or have [him] killed; or by supporting the party of the seducible I shall raise a revolt in his fort, country or camp; or by aupaniṣadika (upaniṣad-type) applications of weapon, fire and poison I shall kill [the one] near, as desired; or by an application of contrivance presided over by myself I shall bring him to loss and expenditure; or, in his group of allies or in [his] army, [when] afflicted by loss, expenditure and absence from home, I shall in due order obtain secret instigation; or by destruction of the supply line, reinforcements and foraging force I shall make a restraint of his camp; or, having raised a weak point by bringing up the army, I shall strike with the whole mass; or, [his] energy struck back, I shall obtain a treaty as desired; or, of [one] bound to me, revolts will arise on all sides; or I shall have his base, [being] without reinforcement, destroyed by allies, forest tribes and armies; or, staying here, I shall protect the acquisition and security of a great region; my army, self-dispersed or dispersed by an ally, [standing] in one [place], will be unbearable for [me] staying here; or my army, skilled in battle on low ground, in pits and at night, free from hindrance of the road, will do action in [the one] near; or [one] who has come here, [to an] unfavourable region and time, will not be, by himself indeed, through loss and expenditure; this region [is] one to be approached through great loss and expenditure, because of the abundance of forts, forests and places of retreat; for the others [it is] mostly disease, and [it is] one with ground not obtained for the exertions of armies; one fallen into adversity will enter it, or, having entered, will not come out.”

text_flags.why: likely typo: ra and a transposed (kāraṇa 'reason'); the sense 'by these reasons' needs kāraṇaiḥ

notes: Lone '-' tokens at line ends are the e-text's continuation marks between the clauses of the quoted speech; the Hindi and English render them as clause breaks. The speech is the weak king's, addressed to the stronger king whose protection he seeks; 'tad' (n. acc.) has no clear referent (possibly the 'human fort' of unit 11, the strong king; or an adverb 'then/therefore'), rendered literally 'that'. Doubtful points: (1) pratipādayiṣyāmi (caus. prati-√pad) rendered 'produce' (glossary 3.11); the sense 'set up against him' is likely, the recipient is not stated. (2) aupaniṣadika = 'of the upaniṣad kind' (secret); praṇidhāna = application, placing; yoga-praṇidhāna rendered 'application of contrivance' (yoga as in 12.4), the sense could also be 'employment of agents'. (3) āsannam = 'the one near' (neighbour or one close by). (4) pratihata-utsāhena (instrumental) is taken as 'his energy struck back'; alternatively my own energy. (5) vadha rendered by 'destruction' for objects (supply line etc.), 'killing' possible. (6) daṇḍa-upanaya = bringing up the army; alternative: bringing him under force. (7) ihasthasya taken as genitive agreeing with the 'me' of me sainyam ('of [me] staying here'), ambiguous; ekastha = standing together in one place; aviṣahya = unbearable. (8) nimna-khāta-rātri-yuddha = battle on low ground, in pits, at night. (9) pathya-ābādha: pathya = of the road (also 'wholesome'); ābādha = hindrance. (10) 'kṣaya-vyayābhyāṃ na bhaviṣyati' literal 'will not be through loss and expenditure', probably 'will perish of itself'. (11) pareṣāṃ vyādhi-prāyaḥ sainya-vyāyāmānām alabdha-bhaumaḥ ca: nominatives taken as describing the region (ayaṃ deśaḥ): 'mostly disease for the others, and with ground not obtained for army exertions'; the exact sense of alabdha-bhauma is uncertain. (12) sāmanta = neighbouring chief, āṭavika = forest chief, tat-kulīna = member of his family, aparuddha = prince in disfavour; mitra-varga = group of allies; skandha-āvāra = camp; kopa = revolt; upajāpa = secret instigation. The closing iti closes the quoted speech and is not rendered.

words.gloss: in the absence of a reason

hindi: “कारण के अभाव में अथवा सेना की वृद्धि में दूसरे के दुर्ग को छोड़कर चला जाए
english: “In the absence of a reason or in the rise of army, having abandoned the other's fort, [he] should go away
notes: Opening of a quotation of the teachers that runs through units 13-15 (closed in unit 15); not a text_flag. 'parasya' is literally 'of the other' (pare = the others, 9.2); here the enemy is probably meant. bala-samucchraya = rise (lit. high uprising) of army, whose army is not stated (the enemy's, or one's own). unmucya = having let go, abandoned.

hindi: अथवा अग्नि में पतंगे के समान शत्रु में प्रवेश करे
english: or [he] should enter the enemy like a moth [into] fire
notes: Quotation of the teachers continued from unit 13. agni-pataṅgavat = like a moth (goes into) fire; 'into' is supplied.

words.gloss: success of one or the other
of [the one] who has abandoned himself

hindi: क्योंकि स्वयं को त्याग चुके की किसी एक की सिद्धि होती है,” ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: for [the one] who has abandoned himself has success of one or the other,” say the teachers.
notes: Closes the quotation opened in unit 13: “... ,” say the teachers (glossary 3.5). bhavati with genitive = 'has'. anyatara = one of two (victory or defeat is not stated). tyakta-ātman = who has abandoned himself (ātman = self).

hindi: “नहीं,” ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: “No,” says Kautilya.
notes: Formula 'na iti X' (glossary).

hindi: अपने और दूसरे के सन्धि-योग्य होने को जानकर सन्धान करे।
english: Having perceived the fitness for a treaty of himself and of the other, [he] should join [in a treaty].
notes: sandheyatā = the state of being fit for a treaty (sandheya = to be made a treaty with / fit for a treaty). upalabhya = having perceived (also: obtained, found). sandadhīta is sam-√dhā (join); the object 'treaty' is not stated in the Sanskrit and is bracketed in English; Hindi keeps the verb literal (सन्धान करे).

hindi: विपर्यय में पराक्रम से सन्धि अथवा अपसार को पाना चाहे।
english: In the reverse [case], [he] should seek to obtain, by prowess, a treaty or a place of retreat.
notes: viparyaya = reversal, the contrary case (when the fitness for a treaty is not found). vikrama = prowess (also 'attack'). lipseta = desiderative of √labh, 'wish to obtain'.

hindi: या सन्धि के योग्य के दूत को भेजे।
english: Or [he] should send an envoy of [one] fit for a treaty.
notes: The genitive sandheyasya is rendered literally 'of'; the sense is 'to the one fit for a treaty' (an envoy to him) or 'of him' (his envoy), the next unit suggests the envoy sent by that king. Kept literal.

words.gloss: on the word of the queens and princes

hindi: अथवा उसके द्वारा भेजे गए को धन और मान से सत्कार करके कहे — “यह राजा का पण्य-अगार है, यह देवियों और कुमारों का, देवियों और कुमारों के वचन से, यह राज्य और मैं तुम्हें अर्पित हैं।”
english: Or, having honoured with wealth and honour [the one] sent by him, [he] should say: “This is the king's house of wares, this [that] of the queens and princes, on the word of the queens and princes; this kingdom, and I, [are] entrusted to you.”
notes: The closing iti closes the quoted speech and is not rendered. paṇya-agāra = house of wares (warehouse, storehouse); devī = queen (lit. 'lady'). tvad-arpaṇaḥ is singular masculine, agreeing with aham; 'arpaṇa' = placing, entrusting, surrender; the kingdom is carried along ('[are]'). Copula supplied. tena = by him, i.e. the king fit for a treaty of unit 19.

hindi: आश्रय प्राप्त किया हुआ समय-आचारिक के समान भर्ता के प्रति बर्ताव करे।
english: [One] who has obtained refuge should conduct himself towards the master like a samaya-ācārika (one of agreed conduct).
notes: saṃśraya = seeking refuge (Book 7 convention), here the refuge obtained. samaya-ācārika is obscure: samaya = agreement, convention, rule; ācārika = of/practising conduct; rendered literally 'one of agreed conduct' with doubt; commentators may take it as one who follows the agreed rules of conduct (a servant by agreement). bhartṛ = master, lord. samaya-ācārikavat is printed as one word with -vat.

words.gloss: bringing in [a bride], marriage, anointing of a son, horse-wares, elephant-capture, sacrificial session, expedition (compound continues in next token)
amusement, goings (end of the compound begun in the previous token)

hindi: दुर्ग आदि कर्म और आवाह, विवाह, पुत्र-अभिषेक, अश्व-पण्य, हस्ति-ग्रहण, सत्र, यात्रा, विहार और गमन — अनुमति पाया हुआ करे।
english: And works beginning with forts, and bringing in [a bride], marriage, anointing of a son, horse-wares, elephant-capture, sacrificial session, expedition, amusement and goings—[he], permitted, should do.
notes: The token ending in '.-' and the next token vihāra.gamanāni are one dvandva compound broken across a line by the edition's continuation mark (the stray space after '.-' is that mark, not flagged); the two words entries carry the members. Obscure: āvāha (lit. 'bringing in'; the bringing home of a bride) and vivāha (marriage); aśva-paṇya (lit. horse-wares, i.e. trade in horses) and hasti-grahaṇa (elephant-capture) are taken as separate members; sattra rendered 'sacrificial session' (alternative: hiding-place/ambush as in 8.5); yātrā = expedition (5.6); karmāṇi = works (glossary 5.1). The two ca are rendered 'and ... and'.

words.gloss: treaty with the constituent elements standing on one's own ground

hindi: अनुमति पाया हुआ सब करे — अपनी भूमि पर स्थित प्रकृतियों से सन्धि, उपघात, अथवा पीछे हटे हुओं में।
english: Permitted, [one] should do everything—a treaty with the constituent elements standing on his own ground, an injury, or [a matter] among those who have withdrawn.
notes: Obscure and doubtful. The compound ending in sandhim is read 'treaty with the constituent elements standing on his own ground' (sandhi = treaty; alternative 'joining, reconciliation'); upaghāta = injury (of them or to the treaty); apasṛteṣu = among those who have withdrawn (alternative: among spies, apasarpa). Whether sandhim and upaghātam are two alternatives of one list ending in 'vā', and what is governed by apasṛteṣu, is not clear. Kept literal.

words.gloss: [one] whose townsmen and country people are corrupt

hindi: या जिसके नगरवासी और जनपदवासी दूषित हैं, न्याय-वृत्ति वाला दूसरी भूमि माँगे।
english: Or [one] whose townsmen and country people are corrupt, [being] of just conduct, should ask for another land.
notes: duṣṭa = spoiled, corrupt (alternative: hostile). The subject (the one who has taken refuge, whose own townsmen and country people are corrupt) is inferred from the context of units 21-23; the Sanskrit gives no noun. yāceta = ask for, beg. paura = townsmen, jānapada = country people (glossary 8.1).

hindi: दूष्य के समान अथवा गुप्त दण्ड से प्रतिकार करे।
english: [He] should counter like the treasonable, or by secret punishment.

text_flags.why: possible typo: short u for ū; dūṣya (the treasonable) is the technical term, duṣya is not a regular form

notes: dūṣya = the treasonable (glossary 6.2); upāṃśu-daṇḍa = secret punishment (13.5). The object of pratikurvīta is not stated (probably the corrupt townsmen and country people of unit 24). pratikurvīta = counter, requite (alternative: remedy).

words.gram: pres. pass. part. f. acc. sg. √dā

hindi: अथवा मित्र से दी जा रही उचित भूमि को स्वीकार न करे।
english: Or [he] should not accept a fitting land being given by an ally.
notes: ucita = fitting, suitable (alternative: customary, accustomed). mitra = ally (glossary 8.5).

words.gloss: of the counsellor, chaplain, commander of the army and heir-apparent

words.gram: pres. pass. part. m. loc. sg. a-√dṛś

hindi: भर्ता के दिखाई न देने पर मन्त्री, पुरोहित, सेनापति और युवराज में से किसी एक को देखे, और यथाशक्ति उपकार करे।
english: The master not being seen, [he] should see any one of the counsellor, chaplain, commander of the army and heir-apparent, and should help according to [his] power.
notes: adṛśyamāne bhartari is a locative absolute: 'while the master is not seen' (not visible / not accessible). paśyet = should see (alternative: meet, look to). purohita = chaplain (house-priest). yathā-śakti = according to power (ability).

words.gloss: in the divine recitations of benediction

hindi: दैवत स्वस्ति-वाचनों में तत्पर आशीर्वादों का वाचन कराए।
english: In the divine recitations of benediction (svasti), [he] should have blessings intent upon that [one] recited.
notes: daivata = of the deities (divine); svasti-vācana = recitation of svasti (benediction). tat-parāḥ = intent upon that (the referent, presumably the master or the king resorted to, is not stated); the Hindi keeps तत्पर literal. vācayet is causative, 'should cause to be recited'.

hindi: सर्वत्र स्वयं के त्याग के गुण को कहे।
english: Everywhere [he] should speak of the quality of self-surrender.
notes: ātma-nisarga is read as 'surrender (lit. release, giving up) of the self'; nisarga can also mean 'nature' (ātma-nisarga 'one's own nature'); the Hindi uses त्याग because निसर्ग in Hindi means 'nature'. Whether ātma-nisargam qualifies guṇam (a quality of self-surrender) or is an object ('self-surrender as a quality') is unclear. guṇa = quality, merit.

hindi: संयुक्त, बलवान् की सेवा करने वाला, शंकित आदि से विरुद्ध, सेना सहित समर्पण करने वाला, इस प्रकार स्थित, भर्ता के प्रति बर्ताव करे।
english: United [and] serving the strong, opposed by the suspected and others, submitting with his army, thus situated, [he] should conduct himself towards the master.
notes: samyukta-balavat-sevī is obscure: 'united (allied) and serving the strong', or 'serving the strong [one] with whom he is united'. śaṅkita-ādibhiḥ: those suspected and the rest (the instrumental after viruddha = opposed by). daṇḍa-upanata = one submitting with his army (glossary 12.5). Closing verse-like summary of the chapter's section; the unit is a two-line half-verse pair with no embedded marker.
